text:
nina: quick heads-up: customer hit duplicate charge in sampleapp when 429 coincided with token refresh. repro notes incoming.

devin: oh no. can you drop the repro steps? trying to triage whether SDK retry or our sample app pattern is at fault.

nina: repro: 1) trigger rate limit on createOrder -> 429. 2) background auth refresh completes while retry backoff is running. 3) SDK retries immediately after refresh, no idempotency header in sample quickstart. outcome: two orders created.

lee: similar to what I saw in QA last month but with webhooks. logs: `POST /orders 429, auth.refresh(), retry -> 200`, webhook sent twice.

priya: sampleapp snippet today is purposely minimal: `await api.createOrder(payload)` — we avoided headers to keep quickstart tiny.

devin: minimal is fine for demos but dangerous for side-effect endpoints. propose we add a one-line idempotency example + callout.

nina: proposed quickstart change: show a helper and a header, keep it 2 lines. e.g. in JS:```js
const id = uidForAction(userId, payload)
await api.createOrder(payload, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': id } })
```

priya: +1. Also add a small blurb: "Use idempotency for operations that create external side effects." keep it collapsed so it doesn't bloat the page.

lee: SDK-level: we should tighten retry semantics around token rotation. idea: SDK tracks last-refresh-ts per request and if the refresh happened during the pending retry window, treat the retry as "refresh-caused" and only replay if an idempotency key exists OR allowRefreshReplay=true. default allowRefreshReplay=true for DX but document strict mode.

devin: API sketch: `client.call(opts)` where opts can include `idempotencyKey` and `strictReplay: boolean`. If strictReplay=true, after auth refresh SDK will surface an error instead of retrying.

infra: ops note: we can also surface a telemetry flag `refresh_replay_attempted` so customers can detect these races. low overhead.

qa-bot: QA: I'll add a deterministic e2e that simulates 429 + auth rotation. We'll orchestrate order: send requests, pause auth refresh, return 429, then resume refresh and retry. Expectation: with idempotency header -> single order; without -> duplicate.

nina: also a small SDK doc change: recommend exponential backoff with full-jitter and a ceiling like 2s for interactive flows; background batchers can use higher caps.

priya: let's standardize on: base=100ms, cap=2000ms, factor=2, jitter=full. Put defaults in SDK but allow overrides. + document parity across JS/Py/Go.

devin: also add server-side guidance: include `Retry-After` when rate limiting and include `X-Idempotency-Required: true` for certain endpoints if server enforces idempotency keys. helps client logic.

lee: UX quick tweak: quickstart should ask a single checkbox: "Does this call create persistent side effects?" If yes, show idempotency snippet and link to production hardening.

nina: action items: @devin update sampleapp quickstart (small PR), @priya add SDK flag proposal and default backoff values, @lee add e2e to QA harness, @infra add telemetry metric. target: EOD next Wed.

devin: I'll open PR and keep it tiny. linking draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/1290 (WIP).

priya: I'll write SDK CHANGELOG note about `strictReplay` and default backoff settings.

lee: QA will run repro against staging-replay-99 once PR lands. tagging ops for a short window to simulate auth rotation.

infra: ack, will provision a small cluster and a script to flip token on demand. logs streamed to /staging/replays/99.

nina: thanks team. goal: keep quickstart friendly but prevent real data duplication. small changes, big impact. :rocket:
